subject: general
question: A can do a piece of work in 24 days and B can do (2)/(5) of the same work in 12 days. Both work together for 6 days. How much work is still left?
solution:
Given:

A can do a piece of work in 24 days and B can do (2)/(5) of the same work in 12 days.

Both work together for 6 days.

Concept used:

Total work = Work done per day × Total time taken 

Calculation:

B can do (2)/(5) of the same work in 12 days

Hence, time taken by B to complete the work = 12 ÷ (2)/(5) = 30 days

LCM (24, 30) = 120

Let the total work be the LCM of the individual time taken by the workers.

Hence, total work = 120 units

Thus,

A does a day = 120/24 = 5 units work

B does a day= 120/30 = 4 units work

Now, work done by them together in 6 days

⇒ 6 × (5 + 4)

⇒ 54 units

Hence, the remaining work in fraction = {{120 - 54} over 120}

⇒ {{66} over 120} = frac{{11}}{{20}}

∴ frac{{11}}{{20}} work is still left.
